hannah: @here FYI we detected sudden connection churn on ingress in us-west-1 at 08:12 UTC. Health checks showed repeated kube-proxy restarts on several nodes; traffic was automatically routed to backup regional capacity. Customers may have seen short 502/504 spikes. Status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2325000000

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-559 created · severity: high · services: ingress-proxy, hosted-api · start: 2026-09-14T08:12:05Z

rajiv: short timeline: 08:10 control-plane rolling upgrade started -> 08:11 kube-proxy pods on two node pools hit sudden mem growth -> 08:12 ingress-controller detected unhealthy endpoints and shifted routes -> 08:16 autoscaler added replicas in fallback region -> 08:20 replaced affected nodes. Impact window ~8 minutes.

maria: mitigation steps taken: 1) reverted the control-plane patch that changed conntrack thresholds 2) drained and reprovisioned 4 nodes 3) forced ingress roll to rebalance. We also raised HPA min replicas as temporary buffer.

cs: customer comms posted at 08:25 UTC and we queued follow-ups to tenants with sustained errors >0.5%. Draft: "We experienced a brief routing disruption on 2026-09-14 between 08:12-08:20 UTC. Traffic was shifted to fallback capacity and normal service resumed. We're investigating root cause and will share a postmortem."

rajiv: helpful commands: `kubectl -n kube-system describe pod kube-proxy-xyz` and `journalctl -u kubelet --since "1h" | grep -i oom` — no further OOMs after node replacement.

oncall-bot: Current status: mitigated · monitoring · link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2325000000 · postmortem: scheduled 2026-09-15T16:00Z

hannah: Thanks — please add any logs or anomaly charts to the postmortem doc. If you spot residual errors reopen the thread. :eyes:
